neighbours.label: the period of a recurring natural or timed event, at the number or 'few' right after 'every' in 'every N years/minutes', as against 'every' with a non-time noun and one-off events
fire: The geyser near the lodge blows every 40 minutes on most days.
Big floods hit the valley every few centuries, the records show.
This comet swings past the Sun every 76 years or so.
Near the coast the marsh floods every few months during the rains.
Locust swarms appear in the region every few years after wet winters.
Large earthquakes strike this fault roughly every 150 years.
The alarm in the lab beeps every 30 seconds until someone resets it.
Our neighbor's fig tree fruits every two years without fail.
quiet: The geyser near the lodge blew hard on the morning we arrived.
Big floods hit the valley long ago, the old records show.
This comet swung past the Sun last spring and faded quickly.
Near the coast every farmer plants rice during the rains.
Locust swarms appeared in the region after one very wet winter.
A large earthquake struck this fault and cracked the old church.
The alarm in the lab beeped once and then went silent.
Every visitor to our neighbor's garden admires the fig tree.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.5 on the number or 'few' after 'every' when a time unit follows; 'every visitor' and one-off events below 0.2
